recommended_phases.title: Phase 1 — Leave repository: findPendingDecisions access path
recommended_phases.rationale: Innermost dependency of the read half; unit-testable in isolation with a fake Pool through the existing dbPool constructor seam, exactly like the audit findByEntity phase. Adds findPendingDecisions(approverId, client?) to ILeaveRepository and PgLeaveRequestRepository (declared inline in leave.repository.ts, the leave module's existing convention): SELECT the existing COLUMNS FROM leave_requests WHERE approver_id = $1 AND status = 'SUBMITTED' ORDER BY start_date ASC, id ASC, reusing the existing mapRow. No service, no route, no migration, no new column, no shared-types change. The status literal is bound as a parameter from LeaveStatus.SUBMITTED, never a bare string.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2 — LeaveService.cancel: notify the approver inside the existing unit of work
recommended_phases.rationale: The core of the feature and the only change to an existing behaviour. One file (leave.service.ts). Adds the private resolveApproverRecipient(request) helper (APPROVED -> request.approverId; SUBMITTED -> employeeService.getEmployeeById(request.employeeId).managerId; DRAFT -> null) and one extra notificationService.create call inside each of the two existing withTransaction callbacks, with the same client threaded through. The notification carries the request id and the leave type code in title/message and sets relatedEntityType 'leave_request' / relatedEntityId = the request id. The existing CANCEL audit entry is left byte-identical; no new audit action, no second entry. Depends on Phase 1 only for the read half, so it can land independently.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3 — LeaveService.listPendingDecisions
recommended_phases.rationale: One file (leave.service.ts). Adds listPendingDecisions(actor) to ILeaveService and LeaveService: assertAuthenticated, then delegate to repository.findPendingDecisions(actor.id). Read-only — no uow.withTransaction, no client forwarding, no writes, no audit, no notification. The SUBMITTED-only filter lives in the repository SQL, so a cancelled request (in-place CANCELLED, or a GP-008 reversal row that is born CANCELLED) can never appear. Depends on Phase 1.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4 — GET /leaves/pending-decisions route
recommended_phases.rationale: One file (leave.routes.ts). Registers GET /leaves/pending-decisions inside the existing leaveRoutes(fastify) function, mirroring the existing GET /leaves handler exactly: resolveActor(request) -> leaveService.listPendingDecisions(actor) -> reply.status(200).send(rows); on throw request.log.error(error) then sendError(reply, error). No controller file, no role guard, no SQL, no business logic. The path is NOT added to PUBLIC_PATHS, so it inherits the existing registerAuth preHandler. Depends on Phase 3.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 5 — Tests: approver notification + pending-decisions read
recommended_phases.rationale: Two test files, no production change. (a) tests/unit/modules/leave/leave.service.test.ts — extend the existing cancel describe blocks with the approver-notification cases: owner cancels SUBMITTED -> exactly one notification to the requester's direct manager carrying the request id and leave type; direct manager / ADMIN cancels APPROVED -> exactly one notification to request.approverId; owner cancels DRAFT -> zero notifications; the notification create receives the same stub PoolClient as the status change and the CANCEL audit entry, inside the single withTransaction callback; the CANCEL audit entry is unchanged. Plus listPendingDecisions cases (delegation, actor id forwarded, empty array is a success). (b) tests/unit/modules/leave/leave.routes.test.ts — a GET /leaves/pending-decisions block over the existing leaveService seam: 200 with rows, 401 UNAUTHORIZED with no actor, and a cancelled request absent from the response. Depends on Phases 1-4.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 6 (optional) — Web approvals queue consumes GET /leaves/pending-decisions
recommended_phases.rationale: Optional, and only if the approver's queue is to be reachable from the UI. web/src/modules/approvals/approvals.service.ts gains a pending-decisions read (or ApprovalsService.listPending switches to the new endpoint) and web/src/infrastructure/api/api-client.ts gains the corresponding IApiClient method. This is the one place the feature touches the second application root, and it is separable: the backend contract is complete without it. Depends on Phase 4.

app_notes:
## Layer boundaries (extend, do not contradict, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md)

- **Presentation** — `src/modules/leave/leave.routes.ts`. Adds one handler, `GET /leaves/pending-decisions`, mirroring the existing `GET /leaves` handler exactly: `resolveActor` → service → `reply.status(200).send(rows)`, `try/catch → request.log.error → sendError`. No controller file (the codebase's binding convention), no SQL, no role branch, no business logic.
- **Application** — `LeaveService.cancel` (extended) and `LeaveService.listPendingDecisions` (new), both declared on `ILeaveService` before implementation. `cancel` keeps ownership of the unit of work; the approver notification is one more step inside the two existing `uow.withTransaction` callbacks, with the same `client` threaded through. `listPendingDecisions` is read-only: no transaction, no client, no writes.
- **Domain** — `LeaveRequest` (unchanged shape), `Notification` (unchanged shape), `LeaveStatus`/`LeaveTypeCode`/`EmployeeRole`/`AuditAction` in `src/shared/types/`. **No new type is introduced by this feature**, so nothing is added to `src/shared/types/` — the approver notification payload is composed inline in `leave`, exactly as the existing approve/reject/cancel notifications are, and `listPendingDecisions` takes no query DTO. This is a deliberate application of the placement rule, not an omission.
- **Infrastructure** — `PgLeaveRequestRepository.findPendingDecisions` (the only new SQL), `PgNotificationRepository` (unchanged), `src/shared/db` pool + `PgUnitOfWork`.

## Dependency direction

`leave` remains the sole orchestrator and the only module that changes. Every edge this feature uses already exists (`leave → notification, employee, audit, balance, validation, policy, shared-types, shared-errors, shared-db, shared-auth`); **no new edge is added and no cycle is introduced**. `notification`, `employee`, `audit`, `balance`, `validation`, `policy`, `leave-type` and the `shared-*` foundations are consumed through their public entry points and are unchanged. Verified: no module depends back on `leave`; the web root's `web-presentation-pages → web-approvals → web-leave → web-infrastructure-api → web-shared-types` chain is untouched by Phases 1–5.

## Concerns surfaced against the existing architecture (not silently resolved)

1. **`GET /leaves/pending-decisions` does not exist.** The feature is phrased as "must *stop* listing a request once it is cancelled", implying an existing endpoint. There is no such route, no `listPendingDecisions` method, and no repository query in the codebase — the leave module exposes only `POST /leaves`, `GET /leaves`, `GET /leaves/:id`, `GET /leaves/:id/history`, and the four state transitions. This feature therefore **creates** the endpoint rather than amending it, and its full contract (membership, ordering, ADMIN scope) is undecided — see openQuestions.
2. **`approver_id` is null on a SUBMITTED request.** `approverId` is only written by `approve`/`reject`. A queue keyed on `approver_id = actor.id` would therefore always be empty for SUBMITTED rows. The queue must be keyed on the requester's `managerId` (the same resolution the notification uses), or the two halves of this feature will disagree about who the approver is.
3. **GP-008 reversal.** Cancelling an APPROVED request does not mutate the original — it inserts a new CANCELLED reversal row and leaves the original APPROVED. The approver notification must therefore be addressed to the **original** row's `approverId` and carry the **original** request id (matching the existing CANCEL audit entry, which is keyed to the original). The reversal row is born CANCELLED, so it can never appear in the queue.
4. **The existing requester notification.** `cancel` already creates exactly one notification to the requester, and the existing unit tests assert exactly one `notificationService.create` call. Adding an approver notification changes that fixed contract — see openQuestions.
5. **`Notification` has no leave-type field.** The requirement that the notification "carry the request id and the leave type" cannot be met structurally without a schema change — see openQuestions.
6. **GP-002 is satisfied without change.** The existing CANCEL audit entry is kept byte-identical; the notification is not an audit record and does not replace one. GP-001 holds (the new read goes through `ILeaveRepository`). GP-005 holds (the new endpoint is not added to `PUBLIC_PATHS` and inherits `registerAuth`; RBAC stays in the service, never inline). GP-006 holds (the route's `try/catch` is unchanged in shape).

open_questions.question: For a SUBMITTED cancellation, what is the approver when the requester has no direct manager (employee.managerId is null)?
open_questions.impact: The notification recipient is undefined for such a request. The feature says "the requester's direct manager", but the codebase already has a null-manager case (the smoke seed's employee has manager_id null, and the GP-008 smoke stage had to seed a separate ADMIN precisely because no direct manager exists). If this is not decided, the implementation will silently skip the notification (a cancelled request with no record of the attempt — the exact failure the feature exists to prevent) or throw and roll back the whole cancellation.
candidate_options: Skip the notification when managerId is null (cancellation still succeeds; no notification row)
Fall back to notifying every ADMIN (requires a new employee lookup by role)
Throw ConflictError and refuse the cancellation (a SUBMITTED request with no manager is undecidable anyway)
Treat it as a data-integrity error and let the transaction roll back

open_questions.question: For an APPROVED cancellation, what is the approver when request.approverId is null?
open_questions.impact: approverId is nullable on LeaveRequest and is only populated by approve/reject. A row that reached APPROVED by any other path (seed data, direct SQL, a future import) has approverId null, so the "recorded approverId" recipient does not exist. Same failure mode as the null-manager case: either a silently skipped notification or a rolled-back cancellation.
candidate_options: Skip the notification when approverId is null
Fall back to the requester's current direct manager
Throw ConflictError and refuse the cancellation
Backfill approverId on approve only and treat null as impossible (assert and fail loudly)

open_questions.question: Does the approver notification replace or accompany the existing requester cancellation notification?
open_questions.impact: The existing cancel path already creates exactly one notification to the requester, and the existing unit tests assert exactly one notification create call. The feature says "send one notification to the approver" without saying whether the requester notification stays. If it stays, the existing tests' "exactly one notification" assertions must be relaxed to "exactly two, one per recipient" — a change to a fixed contract that must be decided, not discovered mid-implementation.
candidate_options: Keep the existing requester notification and add a second one to the approver (two rows per cancellation)
Keep the requester notification and add the approver as a second recipient on the same notification (requires a recipient list, which the notifications table does not have)
Replace the requester notification with the approver notification (a behaviour change to an existing, tested contract)
Keep the requester notification and add the approver notification only for SUBMITTED/APPROVED, leaving DRAFT with the requester notification only

open_questions.question: Where does the leave type code live on the approver notification — a new column, or the message text?
open_questions.impact: The feature requires the notification to "carry the request id and the leave type so the approver can act without a second lookup". The Notification model has no leave-type field — only recipientId, type, title, message, relatedEntityType, relatedEntityId. The request id fits relatedEntityId; the leave type has nowhere structured to go. If it is only interpolated into the message string, the requirement is met in prose but not in data, and any consumer must parse text.
candidate_options: Add a nullable related_leave_type_code column to notifications (a migration, and the first notification field that is not a generic linkage)
Encode the leave type in the message text only (no schema change; not machine-readable)
Encode it in the title, e.g. 'Leave request cancelled (annual)'
Add a generic metadata JSONB column to notifications for future payloads

open_questions.question: What exactly does GET /leaves/pending-decisions return, and in what order?
open_questions.impact: The feature only says the endpoint "must stop listing a request once it is cancelled". It does not say what the queue contains, in what order, or whether it is paginated. The choice determines the repository SQL and whether the endpoint can ever return a row the approver cannot actually decide (approver_id is null until a decision is made, so a SUBMITTED request has no recorded approver — the queue must therefore be keyed on the requester's managerId, not on approver_id, or it will always be empty).
candidate_options: Return all SUBMITTED requests where approver_id = actor.id, ordered by start_date ASC (oldest first, most urgent)
Return all SUBMITTED requests where approver_id = actor.id, ordered by start_date DESC (matching findByQuery's existing ordering)
Return SUBMITTED requests where approver_id = actor.id OR (approver_id IS NULL AND the requester's managerId = actor.id), covering pre-approval rows
Return SUBMITTED requests where approver_id = actor.id, with limit/offset query params

open_questions.question: Does an ADMIN's pending-decisions queue contain every SUBMITTED request, or only their own direct reports'?
open_questions.impact: The existing decide rule lets an ADMIN approve any SUBMITTED request (exempt from the direct-manager check), while the existing visibility rule lets an ADMIN see everything. If the queue is keyed on the requester's managerId, an ADMIN's queue is empty even though they can decide anything — the endpoint would contradict the authority the service grants. This must be decided once, because the same rule governs both the repository filter and the notification recipient fallback.
candidate_options: ADMIN sees every SUBMITTED request (consistent with the existing list/getById visibility rule)
ADMIN sees only requests where they are the requester's direct manager (consistent with the decide rule, which exempts ADMIN from the direct-manager check)
ADMIN sees an empty queue (the endpoint is a manager tool)
ADMIN sees every SUBMITTED request, and the response marks which ones they may actually decide

auth_contract: request.user: { id: string; role: EmployeeRole } where EmployeeRole = 'EMPLOYEE' | 'MANAGER' | 'ADMIN'. Identity and role come from a JWT bearer token verified by the existing registerAuth preHandler (src/shared/auth/index.ts), which populates request.user from payload.sub (id) and payload.role; only /auth/login is in PUBLIC_PATHS. GET /leaves/pending-decisions is NOT added to PUBLIC_PATHS, so it requires a valid token. The route-level resolveActor helper (reused unchanged from leave.routes.ts) extracts request.user and enforces id presence plus EmployeeRole membership at the API boundary, throwing UnauthorizedError on a missing/invalid actor. RBAC is enforced in the service, never inline in the route: LeaveService.listPendingDecisions calls assertAuthenticated and scopes the queue to actor.id; LeaveService.cancel keeps its existing assertCanCancel (owner for DRAFT/SUBMITTED; direct manager or ADMIN for APPROVED). No new role, no new claim, no change to the identity shape. The approver notification recipient is resolved server-side from the request row (APPROVED -> request.approverId; SUBMITTED -> the requester's direct manager via employeeService.getEmployeeById) and is never taken from the caller.
error_response_contract: Errors return { error: string; code: string } via the existing sendError helper (AppError -> its statusCode + code; any other throw -> 500 { error: 'Internal Server Error' }). For GET /leaves/pending-decisions: validation failure -> 400 (ValidationError, code VALIDATION) — the endpoint takes no input, so this is not produced; authentication failure -> 401 (UnauthorizedError, code UNAUTHORIZED) for a missing or invalid actor; authorization failure -> 403 (ForbiddenError, code FORBIDDEN) — not produced, the queue is scoped to the caller rather than refused; not found -> 404 (NotFoundError, code NOT_FOUND) — not produced, an empty queue is a valid 200 with []. Success: 200 with an array of LeaveRequest rows (possibly empty). For POST /leaves/:id/cancel the existing contract is unchanged: 400 validation, 401 missing/invalid actor, 403 ForbiddenError from assertCanCancel, 404 NotFoundError for an unknown id, 409 ConflictError for an already-begun leave or an already-reversed APPROVED request, 200 with the cancelled (or reversal) row on success. A failure to insert the approver notification is not mapped to a new status: it throws inside the unit of work, the transaction rolls back, and the caller receives the underlying error (500) — the cancelled request is never left committed without its notification record.
